newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gilt prices end up on new bond, call easy.
newsitem.headline: Indian gilt prices end up on new bond, call easy.

text.p: Indian government securities ended up in active trade Thursday as the yield curve realigned itself after a bond auction, dealers said.

Prices reacted sharply after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Wednesday set a yield of 11.83 percent against market expectations of 11.90-11.95 percent, at a 30 billion rupee auction of six-year bonds.
"Prices went up for securities of all maturities today as bonds were repriced after yesterday's auction," said a dealer. "But most of the action was in bonds with tenors up to 2004."
He said there was some demand in the morning for the 11.83 percent 2003 bond auctioned at par on Wednesday.
"Some early demand from bidders who were unsuccessful yesterday pushed prices up to 101.35 rupees in the morning," the dealer said. "But demand (for the new bond) fizzled out later."
Among actively-traded securities, the 12.59 percent 2004 stock traded at 104.10 in the morning before dropping to 103.95 in afternoon trade, dealers said. It was traded at 102.90 on Wednesday.
The 12.14 percent 2000 traded at 104.18 against 103.40 and the 13.85 percent 2000 at 108.90 against 107.92, dealers said.
Among treasury bills, the latest 364-day bill yielded 7.90 percent against its Wednesday auction yield of 8.55 percent.
Prices of government securities will rise on Saturday on demand fuelled by low call money rates but the rise will be less than on Thursday, dealers said.
Banks in India's commercial capital of Bombay and some other centres are closed for a Moslem festival on Friday.
"The sharp rise today was a reaction to yesterday's auction result," said a dealer. "Most bonds have been repriced and the rate of rise will be less on Saturday."
Dealers said call money eased to end Thursday at 0.5-1.0 percent, against opening quotes of 4.0-4.5 percent.
"There was little trade today as it is the reporting day," said a dealer. "Some lenders quoted higher, hoping to push rates up but there were few takers."
The dealer said he expected call money to trade between 2.0 percent and 3.0 percent on Saturday.

"Call will be slightly higher due to the outflows towards the new bond," he said. "But liquidity remains good...there were bids for 130.45 billion rupees at yesterday's auction against a notified amount of 30 billion."
"Call money rates should not go up much."
